unit.title: Disconnect and reconnect fixed wired electrical machinery appliance and fixtures

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A hotel in Negril asks you to replace a fixed-wired 220 V water heater. What should you check before the day of the job?
options: That the plumber will connect the cables as well
That the old heater is the same colour as the new one
The new nameplate rating against the circuit
That the hotel has a spare heater for its guests

questions.stem: Why must the people using a building be told before fixed equipment is disconnected?
options: So they can plan for being without it
So they can watch the work being done closely
So they can sign for the new equipment early
So they can switch the supply back on later

questions.stem: A 220 V water heater in Jamaica is fed from a two-pole breaker. Why must both poles be switched off?
options: Only one pole carries current when it is on
The neutral carries the full 220 V when off
The breaker only locks with both poles down
Each line is live at 110 V to earth

questions.stem: A fixed machine has a lockable local isolator and a breaker at the board. Which is the right way to isolate it for work?
options: Switch it off at the on/off switch on its front panel
Lock off its isolator, tag it and prove dead
Take out the control circuit fuse inside the machine
Press the emergency stop and hold it down with tape

questions.stem: You are proving dead at the terminals of a fixed 220 V appliance. Which tests should you make?
options: Only line to line, as that is the 220 V
Between every pair, earth included
Only each line to earth, as that is the 110 V
Only on the conductor the breaker label names

questions.stem: An air-conditioning outdoor unit has been isolated. Which part may still hold a dangerous charge?
options: The guard over the fan
The insulation on the copper pipes
The rubber feet under the unit
The run capacitor

questions.stem: An air-conditioning unit must be disconnected and moved to another room. Who should deal with the refrigerant?
options: A technician certified to handle refrigerant
Any electrician who has the right spanners
The customer, by opening the valves slowly
Nobody, as the gas can be let out into the air

questions.stem: Before disconnecting a motor's terminal box, what is the best record to make?
options: A note of the colour of the motor's paint
The time the motor was switched off
Photos and a labelled sketch of every connection
The motor's weight and the size of its feet

questions.stem: Why are the position of the links in a motor terminal box noted before they are removed?
options: They show who last worked on the motor
They are made of brass and may be sold
They hold the terminal box lid in place
They set how the windings suit the supply

questions.stem: How should conductors be marked as they are taken off the terminals of a fixed appliance?
options: With a pen mark on the wall beside the appliance
By twisting the conductors together in a bunch
With a label naming the terminal each came off
By cutting each one to a different length

questions.stem: A light fitting is taken down and will not be replaced for a week. How should its circuit conductors be left?
options: Bent back into the ceiling with the circuit on
Isolated, ends boxed in connectors, labelled
Wrapped in tape and left hanging from the ceiling
Pushed into the hole and the hole plastered over

questions.stem: A machine is removed for good and will not be replaced. What is the best way to deal with its supply circuit?
options: Disconnect it at the board and make the cable safe
Leave the cable live in case it is needed again
Cut the cable flush with the wall and leave it
Switch off the breaker and leave the cable as it is

questions.stem: When disconnecting fixed equipment, which conductor is usually disconnected last?
options: The protective earth
The neutral
The line
Any of them

questions.stem: When reconnecting fixed equipment, why is the earth conductor usually connected first?
options: It is the easiest one to reach in the box
So the case is earthed before any line
So the tester can be clipped onto it later
Earth terminals are always at the top

questions.stem: A 45 kg pump must be lifted off its base after it is disconnected. What should the team leader plan?
options: One strong person to lift it straight up
To roll it off the base onto the floor
Two people or a lifting aid, and a clear route
To leave it for the customer to move later

questions.stem: Before unbolting a ceiling fan for replacement, what must be planned as well as isolation?
options: Running the fan for a minute to cool it down
Taping the blades together so they do not turn
Asking the customer to hold the ladder steady
Support for its weight as the fixings come out

questions.stem: A new heater's nameplate says 4500 W at 220 V. The circuit has a 20 A breaker. What should you conclude?
options: The circuit is too small and must be upgraded first
The circuit is fine, as 4500 W is a normal heater
The breaker should be swapped for a 40 A one only
The heater should be connected to 110 V instead

questions.stem: A replacement motor's nameplate shows 220 V, but the old one was 110 V. What should you do?
options: Connect it to the old circuit, as motors adjust
Stop and check the supply and circuit first
Connect it and see whether it runs properly
Fit a larger breaker so it does not trip

questions.stem: An air-conditioning unit's nameplate gives a maximum breaker size of 25 A. Which breaker may protect it?
options: Any breaker above 25 A, to stop nuisance trips
A 32 A breaker, which is the next size up
No more than 25 A, and matched to the cable
A 63 A breaker, the same as the main switch

questions.stem: A new appliance draws more current than the one it replaces. What must you check about the existing cable?
options: That its sheath colour matches the new appliance
That it is long enough to reach the new terminals
That it was made by the same maker as the appliance
That its current rating and voltage drop still suit

questions.stem: A trainee tightens every terminal screw as hard as he can. Why is it better to use the maker's torque?
options: Hard-tightened screws are quicker to undo later
The maker's torque makes the screw heads line up
Torque settings are only needed on new equipment
Over-tight can damage; loose joints overheat

questions.stem: When reconnecting a fixed appliance, why must the cable sheath go inside the gland or cord grip?
options: So the sheath keeps the terminals cool
So the cable looks tidy from the outside
So the grip holds the sheath, not the cores
So the earth conductor can be left out

questions.stem: The isolator for an outdoor air-conditioning unit in Montego Bay must be replaced. Which type is suitable?
options: An indoor switch with tape over its cover
A weatherproof, lockable isolator
A plug and socket left lying on the ground
A light switch fixed under the unit's cover

questions.stem: Why must a motor's direction of rotation be checked after it is reconnected?
options: Pumps and some fans are harmed by running backwards
Motors use more electricity when they run backwards
The nameplate must be read while the motor turns
Backward rotation makes the motor run more quietly

questions.stem: At the Centre, who should carry out the short start (bump test) to check a reconnected motor's rotation?
options: The instructor, with guards on and people clear
Any trainee, with the guards taken off to see
The customer, while the team watches from afar
The newest trainee, so they gain experience

questions.stem: A motor's overload relay must be set after reconnection. What value is it usually set to?
options: Twice the breaker rating on the board
The highest number on the relay's dial
The full-load current on the nameplate
Half the motor's starting current

questions.stem: In which order are the checks done after reconnecting fixed equipment?
options: Switch on first, then do dead tests if it fails
Function test, then dead tests, then switch on
Switch on, then inspect, then do dead tests
Inspect, dead tests, switch on, function test

questions.stem: A heater element and thermostat have been reconnected. Before the supply goes on, how can you check the element circuit is complete?
options: Look for a glow when the breaker is switched on
Measure resistance across its supply terminals
Touch the element to feel whether it is warm
Listen for a click from the thermostat when on

questions.stem: About what resistance should a 3 kW, 220 V heater element read when cold?
Ten 36 W fittings on a 110 V lighting circuit are replaced with ten 18 W LED fittings. By about how much does the current fall?
Old fluorescent tubes removed in a lighting changeover contain mercury. How should they be handled?
options: Keep them whole and send them for proper disposal
Break them into a bin so they take less space
Bury them behind the building with the rubble
Leave them in the ceiling for the next electrician

questions.stem: A metal-bodied light fitting is being replaced. What must be connected to its earth terminal?
options: The neutral of the lighting circuit
The circuit's protective earth conductor
The switched line from the light switch
Nothing, if the fitting has a plastic lens

questions.stem: The old fitting's cable has brittle, cracked insulation near the lamp holder. What should you do?
options: Wrap the cracked part with tape and refit
Reconnect it, as the new fitting runs cooler
Report it and replace the damaged part first
Push the cracked part back into the ceiling

questions.stem: A trainee has disconnected a pump but left the cable ends bare and unlabelled. What should you do?
options: Leave them, since the breaker is switched off
Finish the job yourself and say nothing
Tape the ends together and move on
Stop the work and have the ends made safe

questions.stem: How should the team leader hand a reconnected machine back to its operator?
options: Explain the work, show it running and record it
Leave a note on the machine and go home
Tell the operator to try it when they have time
Switch it on and leave before it is tested

questions.stem: A water heater is replaced with a larger one on an upgraded circuit. Why must the board's circuit chart be updated?
options: So the customer knows the price of the heater
So it shows the true load and breaker
So the plumber can find the hot water pipes
So the old heater's serial number is kept

questions.stem: A new water heater has been connected. Why must it be full of water before its supply is switched on?
options: So the thermostat can be set by the plumber
So the breaker does not trip on start-up
The element burns out if powered while dry
So the water pressure tests the cable

questions.stem: What should the job record for a disconnection and reconnection include?
options: Only the time the team arrived on site
The customer's opinion of the new appliance
The make of the tools that the team used
Isolation, connections, tests and names

questions.stem: While disconnecting an old fitting, you find a joint wrapped only in tape inside the ceiling. What should you do?
options: Remake it in a proper enclosure and report it
Add more tape so that it is safer than before
Leave it, because it is not part of your job
Cut it out and leave the two ends apart

questions.stem: A motor was running just before it was isolated. What else must you allow for before handling it?
options: The motor will be heavier while it is warm
Hot surfaces, and parts that may still be turning
The paint on the motor may still be wet
The nameplate will be too hot to read

questions.stem: The equipment the customer has bought is not the type on the work order. What should you do?
options: Fit it, since the customer has already paid for it
Refuse the job and leave the site at once
Stop and check with the supervisor and customer
Fit the old equipment back and say nothing

questions.stem: You return from a break and find your lock still on the isolator, but the danger tag has gone. What should you do?
options: Carry on, as the lock is still in place
Remove the lock, as the isolation is spoiled
Ask the customer whether anyone touched it
Refit a tag and prove dead again before going on

questions.stem: A replacement unit needs a new cable route through a block wall. What must be done to the hole?
options: Leave it open so the cable can move freely
Sleeve it and seal it, fire-stopped if needed
Fill it with paper and paint over it neatly
Make it as large as possible for future cables

questions.stem: Which PPE is most suitable when taking down a light fitting from a dusty ceiling?
options: Ear defenders and a hard hat only
A welding helmet and leather apron
Safety glasses, a dust mask and gloves
Rubber boots and a high-visibility vest

questions.stem: What should happen to the old equipment removed from a customer's premises?
options: Return it or dispose of it as agreed
Leave it outside the customer's door
Take it home for your own use
Throw it into the nearest gully

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: On a test record, the letters IR are used for which dead test?
A 220 V heater element reads 22 Ω when cold. About what power is it rated at, in watts?
What is the name of the threaded ring screwed into the top of a motor so it can be lifted with a hook?
What is the name of the enclosure with a lid in which disconnected conductor ends are made safe with connectors?
Eight 24 W LED fittings run on a 110 V circuit. What is the total current, in amps, to one decimal place?
What is the name of the lockable switch, close to a machine, used to cut off its supply for work?
What is the name of the rubber or plastic ring fitted in a hole in sheet metal to protect a cable passing through?
What is the name of the turning force, given by the maker, to which a terminal screw is tightened?
On a 220 V circuit in Jamaica fed from a two-pole breaker, what is the voltage of each line conductor to earth?
Twelve 58 W fittings are replaced with twelve 22 W LED fittings. How many watts are saved in total?
What is the name of the drawing made before disconnecting, showing where each conductor was connected?
What is the name of the very short start given to a motor to check which way it turns?
Tests done on reconnected equipment before the supply is switched on are called what kind of tests?
A 4.5 kW heater replaces a 3 kW heater on 220 V. By how many amps does the current rise, to one decimal place?
What do the letters RCBO stand for, for a device that gives earth leakage and overcurrent protection in one?
accepted: residual current breaker with overcurrent protection
residual current circuit breaker with overcurrent protection
residual current circuit breaker with overload protection
residual current breaker with overload protection
residual current breaker with over-current protection

essays.stem: A guest house in Ocho Rios wants its 3 kW water heater replaced with a 4.5 kW model. Explain how you would plan the job, including the checks on the existing circuit. Show your figures.
essays.modelAnswer: I would read the new heater's nameplate and the maker's instructions, then check the existing circuit. The old heater drew 3000 ÷ 220 = about 13.6 A. The new one will draw 4500 ÷ 220 = about 20.5 A. If the circuit has a 20 A two-pole breaker and cable rated for 20 A, it is too small, so the cable and breaker would need upgrading to a size suited to the new load and the run length, with the voltage drop checked. I would check there is a lockable isolator near the heater. I would agree a time with the owner so guests are told there will be no hot water, and arrange for the plumber to drain and refit the heater. I would plan safe isolation at the two-pole breaker and isolator, with lock, tag and proving dead, list the materials and tests, and plan to update the board chart.
markingPoints: Reads the nameplate and maker's instructions
Works out old and new currents correctly (about 13.6 A and 20.5 A)
Concludes whether cable and breaker must be upgraded; checks voltage drop and local isolator
Agrees timing with the owner and coordinates with the plumber
Plans safe isolation, materials, tests and updating the circuit chart

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how you would safely disconnect a fixed-wired motor-driven machine and record its connections so it can be reconnected correctly.
essays.modelAnswer: I would tell the operator and supervisor, and stop the machine with its normal stop control. Then I would isolate it at the lockable isolator, fit my own lock and a danger tag, and check my voltage tester on a proving unit. At the terminal box I would test between all conductors, including earth, then check the tester again. I would check for stored energy, such as capacitors or parts still turning. Before removing anything, I would photograph the terminal box and draw a labelled sketch showing each conductor, the terminal it goes to, and the position of any links. I would label each conductor with its terminal as I take it off, disconnecting the earth last. Then I would make the ends safe: insulated in connectors in a covered box, or kept in the gland and labelled, with the isolation still locked off.
markingPoints: Informs people and stops the machine with its normal control
Isolates, locks, tags and proves dead with the tester checked before and after
Checks for stored energy
Records connections with photos, a labelled sketch and conductor labels, including links
Disconnects earth last and makes the ends safe and labelled

essays.stem: Explain how disconnected conductors should be made safe when equipment is removed for a short time, and when it is removed for good.
essays.modelAnswer: When equipment is removed for a short time, the circuit stays isolated and locked off at its breaker or isolator, with a tag saying why. Each conductor end is fitted with a suitable insulated connector and placed in a junction box or the existing enclosure with its lid on, so nothing is exposed even if the circuit is switched on by mistake. The ends are labelled to show which circuit they belong to and that the equipment has been removed. When equipment is removed for good, the circuit is disconnected at the board, the breaker is removed or marked spare, and the cable is either taken out or terminated safely in an accessible box at both ends and labelled. The circuit chart is updated. Bare ends, taped ends or cables pushed into walls are never acceptable, because someone may switch them on or touch them later.
markingPoints: Short term: circuit kept isolated, locked and tagged
Ends in insulated connectors inside a covered box
Ends labelled with the circuit and reason
Permanent: disconnect at board, remove or terminate cable at both ends, mark spare, update chart
Explains why bare, taped or hidden ends are unsafe

essays.stem: Before connecting replacement equipment to an existing circuit, describe all the checks you would make and why.
essays.modelAnswer: I would read the nameplate for voltage, frequency, phases, power or current and any maximum breaker size, and check it matches the supply, for example 220 V single-phase at 50 Hz. I would work out the current and compare it with the circuit's breaker and the cable's current rating, and check the voltage drop for the length of run. If the new load is larger, the circuit may need upgrading. I would check the breaker does not exceed the maximum the maker allows. I would check there is a suitable local isolator, lockable and of the right IP rating if outdoors. I would check the earthing is present and suitable, and that the equipment's cable entries and glands suit the cable. I would check the fixing surface can take the weight. These checks stop overheating, nuisance tripping, damage to the equipment and danger to users.
markingPoints: Nameplate: voltage, frequency, phases, current and maximum breaker size match the supply
Current compared with breaker and cable rating; voltage drop checked
Local isolator suitable, lockable and IP-rated where needed
Earthing, glands and fixings suitable
Explains the reasons: overheating, tripping, damage and danger

essays.stem: Describe how you would reconnect a fixed appliance, the tests you would carry out before it is switched on, and how it is returned to service.
essays.modelAnswer: With the circuit still isolated and locked off, I would connect the earth first, then the neutral if there is one, then the line conductors, using my connection record. Each conductor would be stripped to the right length, fully in its terminal and tightened to the maker's torque, with the sheath held in the gland or grip. I would check that no strands are loose and that covers and seals are fitted. Then I would do dead tests: continuity of the protective conductor to the appliance's metal parts, insulation resistance between conductors and earth (following the maker's advice for any electronics), and polarity, so the switch and protective device are in the line conductors. I would record the results. Only when every lock has been removed by its owner and the area is clear would the supply be restored by the authorised person, then the function test is done and the appliance is handed over with the records.
markingPoints: Reconnects with isolation in place, earth first, from the connection record
Correct stripping, torque, gland or grip; covers and seals refitted
Dead tests: protective conductor continuity, insulation resistance, polarity; results recorded
Supply restored only after all locks removed by owners and area clear
Function test and handover with records

essays.stem: A pump motor at a water tank in St Ann must be swapped for a new one of the same rating. Describe how you would disconnect and reconnect it, including the checks on the motor.
essays.modelAnswer: I would plan the job with the owner so the pump can be off, and isolate the motor at its lockable isolator, lock, tag and prove dead with a checked tester. I would check any capacitor is discharged. I would photograph and sketch the terminal box, note the links, label the conductors and disconnect them, earth last. The plumber or mechanical fitter would uncouple the pump, and we would lift the motor out safely. Before fitting the new motor, I would check its nameplate matches the old one for voltage, current, speed and power, and set the terminal links to suit the supply. After it is fixed and aligned, I would reconnect earth first, tighten terminals to torque, refit the gland and cover, and set the overload to the full-load current. I would do the dead tests and record them. The authorised person then gives a short start to check the rotation before the pump is filled and run.
markingPoints: Plans with the owner; isolates, locks, tags, proves dead; checks capacitor
Records connections and links; disconnects earth last; safe lifting
Checks new nameplate and sets links to suit the supply
Reconnects correctly; sets overload to full-load current; dead tests recorded
Rotation checked by the authorised person before normal running

essays.stem: Explain the special hazards when disconnecting and reconnecting air-conditioning units, and how you would control them.
essays.modelAnswer: The outdoor unit has a run capacitor and sometimes an inverter board that can hold a charge after isolation, so after locking off and proving dead I would measure the capacitor voltage and discharge it safely with a proper tool if needed. The refrigerant must not be released or handled by the electrician; a certified refrigeration technician must recover it or pump it down before the pipes are disconnected. Units are heavy and often fixed high on walls, so lifting must be planned with two people or a lifting aid, and the access equipment must be safe. The outdoor isolator must be weatherproof and lockable, and in the Jamaican sun and rain its seals and glands need checking. The fan blades and fins are sharp, so gloves are worn. On reconnection, the breaker must not be larger than the nameplate's maximum, and the unit is earthed before anything else.
markingPoints: Stored charge in capacitors or inverter boards: measure and discharge safely
Refrigerant handled only by a certified technician
Weight and height: lifting plan and safe access
Weatherproof lockable isolator; sharp fins and blades
Correct breaker size from the nameplate; earth connected first

essays.stem: Your team must replace 20 fluorescent fittings with LED fittings in an office in Kingston. Explain how you would plan and carry out the changeover safely.
essays.modelAnswer: I would survey the office to find which circuits feed the fittings, check the new fittings' ratings and fixing points, and agree a time when the office is empty or quiet. Each lighting circuit would be isolated at the board, locked off and tagged, and proved dead at each fitting with a tester checked before and after. I would check for neutrals shared with other circuits, since a borrowed neutral can be live even with the circuit off, and isolate those circuits too. Using safe access, the team would disconnect each fitting, record the connections, support it while unfixing, and fit the new one with its earth connected first. Old tubes would be kept whole and stored for proper disposal. After all fittings are in, we would do dead tests, have the supply restored, check every fitting works, update the records and clean up.
markingPoints: Survey of circuits and new fittings; timing agreed with the office
Isolation, lock, tag and prove dead at each fitting, tester checked before and after
Checks for shared (borrowed) neutrals
Safe access, support of fittings, earth first; tubes kept whole for disposal
Dead tests, restore supply, function check, records and clean-up

essays.stem: You lead three trainees on a job to disconnect and reconnect several fixed appliances. Explain how you would supervise them, and where you would set hold points to check their work.
essays.modelAnswer: Before starting, I would brief the team on the job, the risks and the isolation plan, and make sure everyone has a personal lock. I would set hold points where work stops until I check it. The first is after isolation: I watch the proving dead with the tester checked before and after. The second is after the connections are recorded and the conductors labelled, before anything is disconnected. The third is when disconnected ends are made safe. The fourth is after reconnection, before the covers go on, to check terminals, torque, earth and gland. The fifth is the dead test results, before the supply is restored. Between hold points I would watch and help, correct mistakes at once and explain why. I would match tasks to each trainee's skill, and record what each one did for their training record.
markingPoints: Briefing on job, risks and isolation; personal locks
Hold point at isolation and proving dead
Hold points at recording connections and making ends safe
Hold points after reconnection and at dead test results
Corrects and explains; matches tasks to skills; records trainee work

essays.stem: Explain what records you would keep when disconnecting and reconnecting fixed equipment, and why each is important.
essays.modelAnswer: I would keep the isolation record showing which isolator was locked, by whom, when, and when it was removed, so there is proof the work was done safely. The connection record, with photos, sketch and labels, shows how the equipment was connected, so it can be reconnected correctly and checked later. I would record the nameplate details of the old and new equipment and any circuit changes, such as a new cable or breaker size. The dead test results show the equipment was safe before it was switched on and give a baseline for future tests. The board's circuit chart is updated so anyone isolating that circuit later picks the right breaker. Finally, the handover record shows who received the equipment, any advice given and anything still to be done. These records protect the customer, the team and the Centre.
markingPoints: Isolation record: who, which isolator, when
Connection record: photos, sketch, labels
Nameplate details and circuit changes
Dead test results and updated circuit chart
Handover record; explains how records protect everyone

practical1.title: Replace a fixed-wired 220 V appliance on an upgraded circuit
practical1.brief: A training bay holds a fixed-wired 220 V appliance (for example a water heater shell or a heater unit) fed from a two-pole breaker and a lockable local isolator. The bay is not connected to any supply. The assessor gives the group the nameplate of a larger replacement. As a group: (1) work out the old and new currents and decide whether the circuit's breaker and cable must change, using the cable data the assessor gives; (2) write a short method statement with hold points; (3) carry out group isolation: every member fits their own lock to a hasp, the leader tags it and proves dead between every pair of conductors with a tester proved on a proving unit before and after; (4) record the connections with photos, a sketch and labels, disconnect (earth last) and make the ends safe; (5) fit the replacement, changing the breaker and cable if your sums say so, and reconnect (earth first) to the right torque; (6) carry out dead tests (protective conductor continuity, insulation resistance and polarity) and record them; and (7) update the circuit chart. Each member leads at least one step while the assessor watches. The instructor decides whether the finished work is energised on the protected supply. Photograph each stage and hand in the sums, the method statement, the records and the updated chart.
materials: Training bay with a two-pole breaker, lockable isolator and fixed appliance (not connected to any supply)
Replacement appliance or its nameplate, and cable data from the assessor
Spare cable and a two-pole breaker of a larger size from the store
Two-pole voltage tester and proving unit
Hasp, a padlock for each member, danger tags
Low-resistance ohmmeter and insulation resistance tester
Screwdrivers, torque screwdriver, wire strippers, labels and a marker
Connectors and a junction box for making ends safe
Method statement, isolation record, test record and circuit chart
photos: The current sums and the decision on the circuit
The hasp with every member's lock and the tag
The tester on the proving unit, and proving dead at the appliance
The connection sketch and the labelled conductors
The replacement fitted and reconnected, before the cover goes on
The dead tests and the completed test record
checklist: Worked out the currents correctly and made the right decision about the circuit
Fitted their own lock and followed every step of safe isolation in order
Proved dead between all conductors with the tester checked before and after
Recorded connections clearly and disconnected the earth last
Made disconnected ends safe and labelled
Reconnected earth first, to the right terminals, at the maker's torque, with the gland or grip holding the sheath
Carried out and recorded the dead tests correctly
Led their step clearly and checked others' work at hold points
safety: The bay is never connected to a supply during the task; only the instructor may energise it
Lift the appliance with two people or a lifting aid
Wear safety glasses when stripping and cutting conductors

practical2.title: Disconnect and reconnect a motor and change two light fittings
practical2.brief: Part A: a motor (single-phase or three-phase, as the Centre has) is mounted on a base and wired through a lockable isolator and a starter with an overload relay. The bay is not connected to any supply. The group isolates it (each member's lock on a hasp, tag, prove dead with a checked tester), photographs and sketches the terminal box, including the links, labels and disconnects the conductors, and lifts the motor off its base safely. The assessor then changes the links or swaps the motor for a similar one. The group checks the nameplate, sets the links to suit the supply, refits the motor, reconnects it, sets the overload to the full-load current, and does dead tests. The instructor carries out the short start to check rotation on the protected supply. Part B: on a lighting bay, the group replaces two fluorescent fittings with LED fittings, making the ends of a third fitting safe in a junction box as if it were removed for good, and updates the circuit chart. Each member takes the lead for one part of the work. Photograph each stage and hand in the connection records and test results.
materials: Motor on a base, with isolator, starter and overload relay (not connected to any supply)
Lighting bay with three fluorescent fittings (not connected to any supply), two LED fittings
Two-pole voltage tester and proving unit, hasp, padlocks and tags
Low-resistance ohmmeter and insulation resistance tester
Hand tools, torque screwdriver, labels and a marker
Lifting aid or a second person for the motor
Connection record, test record and circuit chart forms
Box or rack to keep removed tubes whole
photos: The motor isolated, with locks and tag on the isolator
The terminal box sketch and photo, showing the links
The motor reconnected, with the overload setting visible
The new LED fittings in place, with earths connected
The third fitting's ends made safe in a labelled junction box
The removed tubes stored whole for disposal
The completed test records and chart
checklist: Followed full safe isolation, with their own lock and the tester checked before and after
Recorded the motor's connections and links accurately
Lifted and handled the motor safely
Set the links to suit the supply and the overload to the full-load current
Reconnected fittings with earth first and terminals tight
Made the removed fitting's ends safe and labelled
Carried out and recorded dead tests
Kept old tubes whole and the area tidy
safety: The bays are never connected to a supply during the task; only the instructor energises the motor for the rotation check
Keep hands and clothing clear of the shaft and coupling at all times
Use a stable platform or steps for the light fittings, with a second person close by
Handle fluorescent tubes carefully and do not break them
